FC_EMPTY_DESC: Add a fixed-code 433 MHz ON/OFF remote switch.
FC_SINGLE_BUTTON_HINT: One physical button: learn one code for ON and OFF. Off = use both ON and OFF codes.
FC_INVERT_HINT: Use when On turns the device Off (swaps which RF code is sent). Buttons stay On / Off.
FC_FIX_TIP_BODY:
• On turns the device Off → Invert ON/OFF
• One button on the remote → Single-button remote
• Separate On and Off buttons → leave Single-button off and learn both
FC_RATE_LIMITED: Wait a moment before sending again
FC_BUSY_LEARNING: Finish or cancel learn before saving.
FC_LEARN_HINT: Listening for a strong 433 MHz signal… hold the remote near the antenna and press the button.
FC_LEARN_PROGRESS: Pulses: %s · RSSI: %s dBm (press remote when ready)
FC_LEARN_FAILED: No valid remote signal. Hold the pool remote near the antenna, set frequency to 433.92 if needed, and press again.
FC_LEARN_FAILED_WEAK: Signal too weak. Hold the remote a few cm from the ESP antenna and press firmly.
FC_LEARN_FAILED_SHORT: Signal too short. Press and hold the remote button for about one second.
FC_LEARN_FAILED_NOISE: Noisy or unusual timing. Move closer, avoid other 433 MHz remotes, and try again.
FC_TEST_HINT: Transmit the learned code without leaving this screen
SHADE_UP_TIME_DESC: How long the motor takes to go fully open (Up).
SHADE_DOWN_TIME_DESC: How long the motor takes to go fully closed (Down).
SHADE_REPORTED_POS_HINT: All types use the same scale as Home Assistant: 100% = open · 0% = closed.
SHADE_CALIBRATE_POSITION_DESC: Set the real % without moving the motor. Same scale for every type: 100% = open · 0% = closed. Apply calibration saves immediately; Save also stores this slider.
SHADE_FIX_TIP_BODY:
• Open moves the wrong way (curtain left↔right, shade up↔down) → Invert direction
• Idle % wrong (open in the room, UI says something else) → Calibrate position
• After that, open still reads near 0% and closed near 100% → Invert % reading
SHADE_POSITION_DESC: Does not change motor direction. Only flips the percentage numbers so the scale stays 100% = open · 0% = closed when the motor reports them backwards. Use after Invert direction and calibration if the % is still reversed.
FLIP_COMMAND_DESC: Only swaps Open↔Close RF commands (curtain left↔right, shade/awning up↔down). Buttons stay Open / Stop / Close. Does not change the 100% open · 0% closed scale.
HINT_REMOTE_ID_TEST:
• Use Open/Close — if nothing moves, this ID is free
• If a motor reacts, use Force Unpair and select that device so its memory can forget this ID

RADIO_TOOLTIP_GPIO_1: The name (e.g., SCLK) refers to the pin on the CC1101 module.
RADIO_TOOLTIP_GPIO_2: The GPIO number (e.g., GPIO18) refers to the physical pin on your ESP32.
RADIO_TOOLTIP_GPIO_3: Refer to the 'pinout' diagram of your specific ESP32 model to locate them.
RADIO_SAFETY_TEXT: I understand the risks of misconfiguring the GPIOs.
RADIO_BASE_FREQUENCY_HELP: Central communication frequency. Standard value: 433.42 MHz. Adjust in minimal increments if reception is poor. Return to 433.42 MHz if in doubt.
RADIO_RX_BANDWIDTH_HELP: Controls the width of the monitored spectrum. Narrower filters out more noise (better range). Wider makes the signal easier to capture.
RADIO_FREQ_DEVIATION_HELP: Determines the gap needed to distinguish data bits. High deviation requires a strong signal. Low deviation increases sensitivity but picks up more noise.
RADIO_TX_POWER_HELP: Transmission power. 10dBm is sufficient for most setups. Only use 12dBm if your hardware specifically supports it.

SCANFREQ_DESC: Scan surrounding frequencies to identify and configure your radio devices.
SCANFREQ_SCAN_DESC: Scanning started. Hold any button on your remote — ESPSomfy finds the best frequency. When you stop, that frequency is applied automatically; Save to keep it.
SCANFREQ_APPLIED: Applied %1 %2 to Radio settings. Save to keep it after reboot.

ROLLING_CODE_DESC: Warning: an incorrect value may break communication with the shade
ROLLING_CODE_WARNING_DESC_1: If this device is already paired with a motor, changing the rolling code will cause it to malfunction. Rolling codes are linked to the remote address, and the motor expects them to be sequential.
ROLLING_CODE_WARNING_DESC_2: If you hesitate even slightly, do not press the red button. Green represents safety — press it, wipe the sweat from your forehead, and follow the normal pairing process.
PAIR_GARAGE_DESC: 3 steps: open motor memory → Prog → confirm.
UNPAIR_GARAGE_DESC: 3 steps: open motor memory → Prog → confirm.
PAIR_SHADE_DESC: 3 steps: open motor memory → Prog → confirm.
UNPAIR_SHADE_DESC: 3 steps: open motor memory → Prog → confirm.
WIZ_GARAGE_STEP_1_1: Open the garage motor’s memory (see the motor manual).
WIZ_GARAGE_STEP_1_2: Memory usually stays open about 2 minutes.
WIZ_GARAGE_STEP_2_1: Tap Prog. The controller sends the pairing signal.
PAIR_GARAGE_STEP_3_1: If the door responded, tap Pairing Successful.
UNPAIR_GARAGE_STEP_3_1: If the door responded, tap Unpairing Successful.
PAIR_SHADE_STEP_1_1: On a remote already paired to the motor, press Prog until the motor jogs once.
UNPAIR_SHADE_STEP_1_1: On a remote already paired to the motor, press Prog until the motor jogs once.
WIZ_SHADE_STEP_1_2: Memory stays open about 2 minutes. Tap Next when ready.
WIZ_SHADE_STEP_1_3: Some motors time out sooner — check the manual if nothing happens.
PAIR_SHADE_STEP_2_1: Tap Prog to send the pairing signal.
UNPAIR_SHADE_STEP_2_1: Tap Prog to send the unpairing signal.
WIZ_SHADE_STEP_2_2: The motor should jog again. Some models need a longer press.
WIZ_SHADE_STEP_2_4: If nothing moved, tap Prog again while memory is still open.
PAIR_SHADE_STEP_3_1: Tap Pairing Successful to save and close.
UNPAIR_SHADE_STEP_3_1: Tap Unpairing Successful to save and close.
LINK_REMOTE_DESC: Link your remote to the device
LINK_REMOTE_DESC_1: Press any button on the remote to link it to this device.
LINK_REMOTE_DESC_2: This will not change the remote's association, and this screen will close once the remote is detected.
REPEAT_REMOTE_DESC_1: Press any button on the remote control to repeat its signals.
REPEAT_REMOTE_DESC_2: Once assigned, ESPSomfy RTS will act as a repeater and repeat all signals from the identified remote controls.
REPEAT_REMOTE_DESC_3: Assign a repeater only when ESPSomfy RTS reliably receives a physical remote control but the motor does not.
REPEAT_REMOTE_DESC_4: Repeating unnecessary radio signals will degrade radio performance, and never assign the same repeater to more than one ESPSomfy RTS device. You would create an insidious echo chamber.
REPEAT_REMOTE_DESC_5: Once a signal is detected from the remote control, this window will close and the remote control signals will be repeated.
LINK_GROUP_DESC: Add a device to this group, one step at a time
LINK_GROUP_STEP_1_1: This adds one device to the group. Follow each step until it finishes.
LINK_GROUP_STEP_1_2: The motor should jog twice: once to open memory, and once to confirm it joined the group.
LINK_GROUP_STEP_1_3: Each device must be added separately. Tap Next when you are ready.
LINK_GROUP_STEP_2_1: Choose the device to include in this group.
LINK_GROUP_STEP_2_3: Only devices not already in this group are listed. A device can belong to more than one group.
LINK_GROUP_STEP_3_1: Press the OPEN MEMORY button above. The selected device should perform a brief jog to confirm its memory is open.
LINK_GROUP_STEP_3_2: If the movement occurred, click YES in the confirmation window to proceed to the final step. Otherwise, click NO and try opening the memory again.
LINK_GROUP_STEP_3_3: Note: the motor should only perform one jog. If it performs several, the memory has been closed by mistake. A confirmation window will appear following your action.
LINK_GROUP_STEP_4_1: Press and hold the PAIR TO GROUP button above to send the group association command. The group radio mode is matched to the selected device so the correct motor joins (already-paired motors with a different bit length will not jog).
LINK_GROUP_STEP_4_2: A confirmation window will appear. If the selected motor performed another jog, click YES. The wizard will then close automatically, and the association will be complete.
LINK_GROUP_MEMORY_READY_FOR_GROUP: Once the device jogs, the motor memory will be ready to add the device to the group.
LINK_GROUP_LINK_DONE: Once the device jogs, it will be added to the group and the process will be complete.
UNLINK_GROUP_DESC: Setup wizard to guide you step-by-step through removing your device from the group
UNLINK_GROUP_TITLE_STEP_3: Unpairing your device from the group
UNLINK_GROUP_STEP_1_1: This wizard will guide you through removing this device from the group. Follow all instructions at each step until the device is removed from the group.
UNLINK_GROUP_STEP_1_2: During this process, the device must perform exactly two jog movements. The first indicates the motor memory is open, and the second confirms the group has been deleted from the motor memory.
UNLINK_GROUP_STEP_1_3: Each piece of device must be removed from the group individually. When you are ready to begin dissociating the device from the group, press the NEXT button to start.
UNLINK_GROUP_STEP_2_1: You must first open the device's memory by pressing the OPEN MEMORY button. The device should perform a jog to indicate the memory is open.
UNLINK_GROUP_STEP_2_2: If the movement occurred, click YES in the confirmation window to proceed to the final step. Otherwise, click NO and try opening the memory again.
UNLINK_GROUP_STEP_2_3: The motor should only perform one jog. If it performs more than one, it means the motor memory has been closed.
UNLINK_GROUP_STEP_3_1: Now you must send the group dissociation command; press the UNPAIR FROM GROUP button above.
UNLINK_GROUP_STEP_3_2: A confirmation window will appear. If the motor performed another jog, click YES. The wizard will then close automatically, and the dissociation will be complete.
UNLINK_GROUP_METHOD_1: If you have trouble getting the motor to react at this stage, you can try opening the memory using a remote control. This is usually done by selecting the channel and then holding the PROG button down.
UNLINK_GROUP_METHOD_2: If you have opened the memory using this alternative method, press the NO button to close this message, then the NEXT button to skip this step.

BT_FORCE_UNPAIR_DESC: Remove this Remote ID from the wrong motor (e.g. curtain still reacts)
FORCE_UNPAIR_DESC: This Remote ID (%1) is in the shade record but may be stored in a different motor. Remove it from that motor, then Pair this shade to the correct one.
FORCE_UNPAIR_STEP_1_NOTE: Example: left blinds use Remote ID 872484 in ESPSomfy, but Open/Close also moves the curtain. The curtain motor learned 872484. Force Unpair removes 872484 from the curtain so you can Pair the blinds cleanly.
FORCE_UNPAIR_STEP_1_A: Do not change the Remote ID unless you want to. This wizard removes the ID from the wrong motor.
FORCE_UNPAIR_STEP_1_B: You will open memory on the motor that currently reacts (curtain), then send PROG for this shade’s Remote ID.
FORCE_UNPAIR_SELECT_HOST: Motor that currently reacts to this Remote ID
FORCE_UNPAIR_SELECT_HOST_HINT: Select the device whose motor jogs when you Open/Close this shade (often the curtain). Memory will be opened with that motor’s own remote, then Remote ID %1 will be removed from it.
FORCE_UNPAIR_STEP_2_A: Choose the motor that wrongly responds to this Remote ID.
FORCE_UNPAIR_STEP_2_B: Press Next when the correct motor is selected.
FORCE_UNPAIR_STEP_3_A: Press Open Memory. Only the selected motor should jog.
FORCE_UNPAIR_STEP_3_B: If it jogged, press Yes to continue. If not, try again.
FORCE_UNPAIR_STEP_3_NOTE: Open Memory uses the selected motor’s remote. The blinds Remote ID is not transmitted yet.
FORCE_UNPAIR_MEMORY_READY: That motor’s memory is open. Next you will unpair this shade’s Remote ID from it.
FORCE_UNPAIR_STEP_4_A: Press Unpair Remote ID. The selected motor should jog again (ID removed).
FORCE_UNPAIR_STEP_4_B: If it jogged, press Yes. Then Pair this shade to the correct blinds motor.
FORCE_UNPAIR_LINK_DONE: If the motor jogged, this Remote ID was removed from it. You can now Pair this shade to the correct device.
MSG_FORCE_UNPAIR_DONE: Force Unpair finished. Pair this shade to the correct motor when ready.
ERR_FORCE_UNPAIR_NO_HOST: Add at least one other device (e.g. the curtain) so you can open its memory for Force Unpair.

MESH_ACTIVITY_HINT: Live RF activity from every radio on the mesh. Shade names match a motor address or linked remote.
MESH_ACTIVITY_EMPTY: No mesh RF activity yet. Press a remote or move a shade.
MESH_NO_REPEATERS: No Repeaters paired yet. Set a second ESP on this network to Repeater and pair it here.
MESH_REPEATERS_HINT: Paired controllers that extend RF coverage.
MESH_ROOM_RADIOS_SHORT: Choose Auto or lock a radio per room.
MESH_ROOM_RADIOS_HINT: Per room: Auto picks the strongest radio that heard a linked remote (≥ −85 dBm). Manual locks that room to This unit or a Slave. If the chosen Slave is offline, the next-best online radio is used, or this Router. Link the physical remote on each shade so Auto can identify it.
MESH_NO_ROOMS: Add rooms on the Somfy tab, then assign a radio here.
MESH_RANKS_HINT: Updated when a motor address or linked remote is heard. Auto mode uses these ranks.
MESH_NO_RANKS: No ranks yet. Press a linked remote.
MESH_WIZARD_DESC: Router is the main unit (shades, Home Assistant, this web UI). Repeater is an extra radio on the same network.
MESH_WIZARD_PAIR: Pick a Router on this network, or type its IP. Use the Router login password (set one on the Router first if it has none).
MESH_NO_ROUTERS: No Routers found yet. Wait a few seconds, or type the IP.
MESH_NEED_PASS: Enter the Router login password (set one on the Router first).
MESH_PAIR_FAIL: Could not pair. Check the IP and password.
MESH_UPDATE_PEERS_DESC: Online Repeaters get the same firmware after this Router.
MESH_OTA_OFFLINE_SKIP: Offline Repeaters were skipped. Update them from Mesh when they are back.
